candidates.title: Disappearance of retired Air Force General Neil McCasland
candidates.place_text: Quail Run Court, Albuquerque, New Mexico (Sandia foothills)
candidates.quote: The trail begins in Albuquerque, New Mexico, in the shadow of Sandia Mountains. It's February [music] 27th, 2026, a late Friday morning on Quail Run Court.

link.reason: Both tell of retired General Neil McCasland going missing from his New Mexico home in 2026.
link.difference: Gives the exact date (Friday morning, 27 February 2026) and the street (Quail Run Court in the Sandia foothills), and credits the 911 call and the sheriff's office.

candidates.title: Susan McCasland's 911 call about her husband
candidates.quote: I have some indication that he must have planned not to be found.

link.reason: Susan McCasland's 911 call is one incident inside the disappearance story, not the whole disappearance, and no story below covers the call itself.

candidates.title: McCasland as Pentagon director of special programs overseeing acquisition SAPs
candidates.place_text: Pentagon, Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition, Technology and Logistics
candidates.quote: From June 2009 to May 2011, McCasslin served as director of special programs at the Pentagon [music] in the office of the under secretary of defense for acquisitions, technology, and logistics.

link.reason: This is McCasland's 2009-2011 Pentagon post as director of special programs. The disappearance story only mentions his SAP oversight role in passing, and no story covers this posting.

candidates.title: Wright-Patterson as alleged home of Roswell crash debris
candidates.quote: Wright Patterson isn't [music] just famous for Project Blue Book. It's the alleged home of the Roswell crash debris.

link.reason: Both tell the same claim: Wright-Patterson is where the Roswell wreckage was supposedly taken.
link.difference: Told as place-lore about the base, with no link to McCasland running the lab, and ties it to Project Blue Book.

candidates.title: Asking General Curtis LeMay to enter the secret room at Wright-Patterson
candidates.quote: I called Curtis Lame and I said, "General, uh, I know [music] we have a room at Wright Patterson where you put [music] all this secret stuff. Can I go in there?" I've never heard him get mad, but he got mad in hell at me.

link.reason: Both are Goldwater's account of asking Curtis LeMay to see the secret room at Wright-Patterson and being cussed out.

candidates.title: Tom DeLonge email to John Podesta about General McCasland
candidates.quote: Buried in that email dump is an email from Tom Dong to Podesta. The subject line, General McCassland Dong writes, he mentioned he's a skeptic. He's not. I've been working with him for 4 months.

link.reason: This is one specific email in the Podesta leak, DeLonge's 'General McCasland' message. The nearest story covers the whole correspondence and the meeting, so it is broader.

candidates.title: Susan McCasland accepted a calendar invite for a DeLonge-Podesta meeting
candidates.quote: a calendar notification shows that Susan herself accepted a Google calendar invite for something called a Dong Podesta meeting.

link.reason: Susan McCasland accepting a calendar invite is a separate document detail inside the Podesta leak. The nearest story is about the correspondence and meeting as a whole.

candidates.title: Susan McCasland's Facebook statement on Roswell bodies and debris at Wright-Patterson
candidates.quote: Neil does not have any special knowledge about the ET bodies and debris from the Roswell crash stored at Wright Pad.

link.reason: Susan's 2026 Facebook statement denying Neil had knowledge of Roswell bodies is a different statement from her tweet about a mother-ship abduction.

candidates.title: Majestic 12 as a cover for continuity of government programs
candidates.quote: And at one point, he admitted that the Majestic 12 was basically just a cover for continuity of government programs.

link.reason: Both tell John Alexander's claim that Majestic 12 was a continuity-of-government program.

downgraded.why: a theory telling and the program story alexander-says-mj-12-was-continuity-of-government: a program and a story of another kind are different grains

candidates.title: L'Espresso article on Trump taking control of special access programs
candidates.quote: In the summer of 2025, the mainstream Italian magazine Let Espresso published an article from a confidential [music] source. It claimed that President Trump was wrestling control [music] of special access programs away from the Pentagon

link.reason: Both tell of the summer 2025 L'Espresso article on the Trump White House and secret programs.
link.difference: Stresses Trump taking control of special access programs from the Pentagon, citing a confidential source, and does not name Project Preserve Destiny.

candidates.title: Project Preserve Destiny
candidates.quote: The genesis of it was in 1947. and we came in contact with an alien species and in 1960 they started a a project. It was called project preserve destiny

link.reason: Dan Sherman's own account of NSA Project Preserve Destiny, beginning with 1947 contact and a 1960 start, almost word for word as the story holds it.
link.difference: Gives 1947 and 1960 as the program's origin dates instead of the story's 1991-1992 dates for Sherman's involvement.

candidates.title: Trump's Truth Social directive to release alien and UAP files
candidates.quote: Trump announced on Truth Social that he was directing the Pentagon and other agencies to begin identifying and releasing government files related to aliens and the UAP phenomena.

link.reason: Trump directing the Pentagon and other agencies to release UAP and alien files is the same 2026 order behind the Department of War file release.
link.difference: Names the Truth Social post as where the directive was made, not the release itself.

candidates.title: The 'association' of 24 retired officials pushing UAP programs back under government oversight
candidates.quote: There has arisen uh an insurgency group that have uh occupied extremely high positions uh in the defense department uh inside the central intelligence agency

link.reason: An insurgency of 24 retired defense and CIA officials trying to bring UAP programs back under oversight is not told by any story; the nearest, DoD officials advising against disclosure, makes a different claim.

candidates.title: DTRA official collecting documents on extraterrestrials
candidates.quote: person in charge of collecting all of the information from Ditra dealing with extraterrestrials and as he put it quote unquote little green men happened to sit next to me at my computer terminal and began pulling all the documents on my system and the systems in our skiff.

link.reason: A firsthand account of a DTRA official pulling ET documents from a SCIF's systems; the DTRA story about AEC records concerns a different claim about what DTRA held.

candidates.title: Tim Burchett on the high rate of researchers disappearing
candidates.quote: He told the Daily Mail that the numbers seem very high in these certain areas of research.

link.reason: Burchett's comment to the Daily Mail about researchers disappearing is unrelated to his ocean-hotspot claims; no story covers it.

candidates.title: TMBB spaceships X account suspected to be McCasland
candidates.quote: After his story broke, an online manhunt zeroed in on a potential smoking gun, an exac account called TMBB spaceships.

link.reason: The online hunt that tied the TMBB spaceships X account to McCasland is not in the corpus; the McCasland stories are about the lab and a calendar invite.

candidates.title: Invention of the Mondaloy superalloy
candidates.place_text: Rockwell Science Center; Air Force Research Laboratory, Wright-Patterson AFB
candidates.quote: The stalemate finally shattered in the 1990s thanks to the hard work of Dallas Hardwick and Monica Resza at the Rockwell Science Center.

link.reason: The development of the Mondaloy superalloy at Rockwell and AFRL does not appear in any story.

candidates.title: Jesse Marcel Jr. on foil-like Roswell debris that would not burn
candidates.quote: In an interview with journalist Bob Pratt, Jesse Marcel Jr., The Army Air Force intelligence officer at the Roswell crash site described some of the debris as thin and foilike, and when he held a lighter to it, it didn't burn.

link.reason: The same Roswell debris, thin as foil, that Marcel handled at the 1947 crash site.
link.difference: Adds that the foil would not burn under a lighter, credits the account to Jesse Marcel Jr. through an interview by Bob Pratt, and calls Jr. the intelligence officer at the site.

candidates.title: Roswell material as seed for an exotic alloy R&D program at Wright-Patterson
candidates.place_text: Air Force Research Lab, Wright-Patterson AFB
candidates.quote: The theory goes that whatever was recovered at Roswell eventually became a classified R&D seed program at Wright Patterson's Air Force Research Lab.

link.reason: A theory that Roswell material seeded a classified alloy R&D program at AFRL; the nearest story says only that the wreckage was rumored to have been taken to the Wright-Patterson lab, not that it started an R&D program.

candidates.title: 1949 Wright-Patterson contract with Battelle on nickel-titanium alloys
candidates.quote: Wright Patterson had [music] a contract with Battel Memorial Institute in 1949 studying nickel titanium alloys

link.reason: The same 1949 contract between Wright Field and Battelle Memorial Institute to study nickel-titanium alloys.

candidates.title: Disappearance of Monica Reza near Mount Waterman
candidates.place_text: Mount Waterman, San Gabriel Mountains, Angeles National Forest, California
candidates.quote: So, let's go back to June 22nd, 2025, when the woman who taught us how to tame fire vanished.

link.reason: Monica Reza's 2025 disappearance near Mount Waterman isn't in the corpus. The Mondaloy story only names her as an inventor in the 1990s.

candidates.title: Disappearance of Los Alamos employee Melissa Casillas
candidates.place_text: Ranchos de Taos, New Mexico / Los Alamos National Laboratory
candidates.quote: Melissa Casillas is a 53-year-old administrative assistant at Los Alamos National Laboratory

link.reason: No story covers the 2025 disappearance of Los Alamos employee Melissa Casillas. The Los Alamos stories are about other events.

candidates.title: Killing of Caltech astronomer Carl Grillmair
candidates.quote: On February 16th, 2026, about 30 mi northeast of Waterman Mountain, where Monica Resza disappeared, another colleague from Caltech and JPL would meet an equally tragic and suspicious end.

link.reason: The killing of Carl Grillmair in 2026 isn't a story of its own. The Loureiro story only mentions Grillmair in passing while it tells a different killing.

candidates.title: Armed trespasser on Grillmair's property in December
candidates.quote: On December 20th, 2025, according to sheriff officials in court records, Carl Gilmer called the police to report someone trespassing on his sprawling lot in Lo.

link.reason: The December 2025 armed trespass on Grillmair's property happened before his killing in telling 3, so it is a separate earlier event.

candidates.title: Oumuamua, the first interstellar object
candidates.quote: In 2017, we discovered Amua Mua, the first ever interstellar object to visit our solar system.

link.reason: Both tell of the 2017 discovery of 'Oumuamua as the first interstellar object.
link.difference: Leaves out Pan-STARRS and Hawaii, and calls it the first interstellar object ever seen in the solar system.

candidates.title: Avi Loeb on the anomalies of Oumuamua
candidates.quote: All the proposals that were put on the table to explain the anomalies of Amua Mua invoked a rock of a type that we've never seen before.

link.reason: This is Loeb's own statement that every natural explanation of 'Oumuamua's anomalies needs a rock of a type never seen before. The quote is nearly identical.

candidates.title: Pentagon review of Vera Rubin Observatory imagery
candidates.place_text: Vera Rubin Observatory; secure facility in California
candidates.quote: All of Reubin's imagery has to be approved by the Pentagon.

link.reason: Both describe the military screening Vera Rubin Observatory data to keep classified objects out of it.
link.difference: Says the Pentagon must approve all Rubin imagery at a secure facility in California, citing an article in The Atlantic.

candidates.title: Air Force censorship of Pan-STARRS imagery
candidates.quote: A much smaller all sky survey called Pan Stars, the same one which discovered AmuA Mua, underwent massive censorship from the Air Force

link.reason: No story tells of the Air Force censoring Pan-STARRS survey imagery. The Pan-STARRS stories are about specific objects it found.

candidates.title: Villarroel's pre-Sputnik transients on Palomar plates
candidates.quote: She found tens of thousands of transients, light reflecting mirrorlike objects orbiting the Earth.

link.reason: Both tell of Villarroel finding tens of thousands of mirror-like transients on the 1949–1957 Palomar plates, before Sputnik.
link.difference: Says outright that the transients are objects orbiting the Earth.

candidates.title: Villarroel on multiple transients appearing and vanishing
candidates.quote: Sometimes you can see multiple of them appearing and vanishing within half an hour.

link.reason: This is a general claim that groups of transients appear and vanish within half an hour. The closest story is one specific case, the five transients of 27 July 1952, so the grains differ.

candidates.title: Murder of MIT plasma physicist Nuno Loureiro
candidates.quote: Except on December 15th, Dr. Nuno Lorero was gunned down inside his Brookline, Massachusetts home.
documents: Department of Justice transcript of Valente videos

link.reason: Both tell of the 2025 shooting of fusion physicist Nuno Loureiro at his home.
link.difference: Places the shooting in his Brookline, Massachusetts home on December 15, names Claudio Valente as the shooter and cites a DOJ transcript of Valente's videos.

candidates.title: Claudio Valente quits his job and vanishes
candidates.quote: One day in 2013, Valente reported to work. He declared it would be his last day.

link.reason: Valente quitting his job at SAPO in 2013 and vanishing is an earlier event in the shooter's life. No story covers it.

candidates.title: Brown University shooting
candidates.place_text: Barus and Holley building, Brown University, Providence, Rhode Island
candidates.quote: Valente executed his plan on Saturday, December 13th, 2025.
documents: Department of Justice transcript of Valente videos

link.reason: The December 13, 2025 Brown University shooting is a separate attack from the Loureiro murder. No story covers it.

candidates.title: Murder of MIT plasma physicist Nuno Loureiro
candidates.quote: Tragically, Nuno Lurero went into surgery that evening, but did not survive. He was pronounced dead the following morning.

link.reason: This retells Loureiro's 2025 death after the shooting.
link.difference: Adds that he went into surgery that evening and was pronounced dead the next morning, and gives the place as Brooklyn, New York.

candidates.title: Theory that shooter Valente was awaiting programmed instruction
candidates.quote: Or maybe he was awaiting instruction, subliminal or conscious instruction.

link.reason: The theory that Valente was waiting for programmed or subliminal instruction is a claim about the shooter's motive. No story is about it.

candidates.title: TAE Technologies–Trump Media merger announced two days after Loureiro's death
candidates.quote: The deal was announced on December 18th, 2025. Lorero died on December 16th.

link.reason: The TAE–Trump Media merger being announced two days after Loureiro's death is a separate timing theory. No story covers it.

candidates.title: GEC Marconi scientist deaths during Star Wars/SDI era
candidates.quote: Between 1982 and 1990, 25 engineers and computer scientists, all working for GEC Maronei on some of Britain's most classified defense projects, all died one after [music] another.

link.reason: The deaths of GEC Marconi scientists in Britain from 1982 to 1990 are not covered. The SDI stories are about funding fronts, not these deaths.

candidates.title: Disappearance of Jacobo Grinberg after lattice discovery
candidates.quote: Take the disappearance of Mexican neurohysiologist and psychologist Jacobo Grinberg, who vanished in 1994, just after his [music] biggest discovery.

link.reason: Both tell of Mexican neurophysiologist Jacobo Grinberg vanishing in the mid-1990s just after reaching his key insight.
link.difference: Dates the disappearance to 1994 rather than 1995 and links it to his lattice discovery, not to Puharich's death.

candidates.title: Disappearance of Malaysia Airlines flight MH370
candidates.place_text: Kuala Lumpur / South China Sea / Indian Ocean
candidates.quote: On March 8th, 2014, Malaysia Airlines flight MH370 took off from Koala Lumpur with 239 people aboard.

link.reason: The 2014 disappearance of MH370 itself is not a story yet. The nearest stories are about the orb videos and the theories built on them, not the flight's disappearance.

candidates.title: Ashton Forbes plasma orb wormhole theory of MH370
candidates.quote: Researcher Ashton Forbes [music] claims that these videos show MH370 over the Nicabar Islands being encircled by three fusionpowered plasma orbs that generate a spinning wormhole teleporting the plane westward

link.reason: Both tell Ashton Forbes's claim that the MH370 videos show the plane being teleported by orbs.
link.difference: Specifies three fusion-powered plasma orbs making a spinning wormhole over the Nicobar Islands that teleports the plane westward toward Diego Garcia.

candidates.title: Freescale Semiconductor engineers aboard MH370
candidates.quote: Among the documented passengers on the MH370 flight were 20 engineers from Freescale Semiconductor,

link.reason: This is a theory about one group of passengers, the 20 Freescale engineers. It sits inside the MH370 disappearance story, which only covers the flight vanishing, so it is a narrower and distinct claim.

candidates.title: Itzhak Bentov's theories shaped CIA Gateway Process and Stargate
candidates.quote: His theories helped shape the foundation of the CIA's gateway process, [music] a protocol developed by consciousness researcher Robert Monroe in Virginia

link.reason: No story covers Bentov's ideas shaping the Gateway Process and Stargate. The Hemi-Sync paper and Monroe stories are about different documents and events.

candidates.title: Bentov killed in American Airlines Flight 191 crash
candidates.quote: Bentoff's life was tragically cut short at 55 years old when American Airlines Flight 191 crashed shortly after taking off from Chicago O'Hare airport,

link.reason: Same event: Bentov's death in a plane crash in 1979.
link.difference: Names the crash as American Airlines Flight 191 out of Chicago O'Hare and gives his age as 55.

candidates.title: Ning Li's gravity research vanishes into classified world
candidates.quote: Her story took an even darker turn in 2014 when she was struck by a car on the University of Alabama campus and suffered permanent brain [music] damage.

link.reason: Same story: Ning Li's gravity research moves into classified work and disappears from public view.
link.difference: Adds that she was hit by a car on the University of Alabama campus in 2014 and suffered permanent brain damage, and runs the timeline up to 2021.

candidates.title: John Norseen at Allagash during 1976 abduction testing subcutaneous tracking device
candidates.quote: He said he was doing a TTR, tag, trace, retrieve exercise with a subcutaneous device that they were testing

link.reason: No story places Norseen at the 1976 Allagash abduction running a tag-trace-retrieve exercise. The only Norseen story is about his biofusion work.

candidates.title: Death of John Norseen
candidates.quote: Norine died while on business for Concurrent Technologies on September 27th, 2007.

link.reason: Norseen's death in 2007 is a separate event from his biofusion program and his contract report.

candidates.title: McCasland and Monica Reza cases possibly connected
candidates.quote: For example, General Neil McCasslin's case seems eerily possibly connected to Monica Resza's.

link.reason: This is a theory linking the McCasland and Reza cases. The existing stories cover each disappearance on its own, not a link between them.

candidates.title: Bush administration officials urged to read The Three-Body Problem
candidates.quote: During the Bush administration, key players in the federal government were urged to read the Chinese science fiction novel, The Threebody Problem,

link.reason: Same story: The Three-Body Problem became required reading for senior US national security officials, as relayed from Pippa Malmgren.
link.difference: Places it specifically during the Bush administration.

candidates.title: Harold Malmgren: NHI track the frontier of human innovation
candidates.quote: Why did a presidential adviser named Harold Melmgrren who worked [music] directly with JFK, LBJ, Nixon, and Ford and who was briefed on UFOs, why did [music] he tell me that this is how the nonhuman intelligences operate by tracking the frontier of human innovation?

link.reason: Malmgren's claim that non-human intelligences track the frontier of human innovation is a different claim from his tweets about the Bissell briefings or the telepathic UFO material.

candidates.title: UFOs at nuclear sites
candidates.place_text: United States and worldwide nuclear sites
candidates.quote: Robert Hastings, the author of the great book UFOs and Nukes, has talked to almost 170 of these people.

link.reason: Same story: Hastings's book UFOs and Nukes and his interviews with about 170 witnesses of UFOs at nuclear sites.
link.difference: Gives the number as almost 170 and extends it to nuclear sites worldwide.

candidates.title: UFO crash next to Brookhaven National Lab
candidates.quote: There was even a UFO crash right next to [music] Brook Haven National Labs.

link.reason: Both tell of a UFO crash at or beside Brookhaven National Laboratory on Long Island.
link.difference: Gives no year, no townspeople witnesses and no claim that the lab recovered the craft; it only says the crash was right next to the lab.

candidates.title: Soviet UFOs during transport of sensitive technology
candidates.quote: Russian General Vasilei Alexv said that UFOs would show up when they transported sensitive scientific technology.

link.reason: Both are General Vasily Alexeyev's public statement about UFOs. This telling gives what he said: UFOs appeared when sensitive technology was being moved.
link.difference: Says what the claim was (UFOs appeared while sensitive scientific technology was being transported) but does not mention the 2000 German magazine.

candidates.title: Obama tells Eddie Vedder to read The Three-Body Problem
candidates.quote: It involves former President Barack Obama and Pearl Jam lead singer Eddie Veter drunk around a campfire.

link.reason: Same anecdote: a drunk Obama at a campfire tells Eddie Vedder to read The Three-Body Problem.
link.difference: Told as the host's own narration and names Pearl Jam.

candidates.title: Scientific discoveries as received revelations
candidates.quote: Whether it's Heisenberg downloading matrix multiplication [music] at Elgoland, Dac staring at the fire at Cambridge and downloading the Dac equation,

link.reason: Same theory that scientific breakthroughs were received like revelations, using the same examples of Heisenberg at Heligoland and Dirac at the fire in Cambridge.
link.difference: Credits Jimena Canales, adds Bohr and Descartes, extends the period back to the 17th century and leaves out Einstein and Pauli.

candidates.title: Death of anti-gravity researcher Amy Eskridge
candidates.quote: One of them is Alabama based scientist Amy Escridge. She was openly studying anti-gravity technology when she died in 2022.

link.reason: Both tell of the 2022 death of anti-gravity researcher Amy Eskridge.
link.difference: Told by a news reporter, places her in Alabama and does not mention the sixth force or directed-energy burns.

candidates.title: Friend spoke to Amy Eskridge hours before her death
candidates.quote: I don't believe that she killed herself. I I just can't because I spoke to her four hours before and she told me time and time again, I'm not going to commit suicide.

link.reason: This is the friend's own firsthand account of talking with Eskridge four hours before she died and doubting it was suicide. That is a different witness's own testimony, not the general story of her death.
